title: quantization-performance-quality-tradeoffs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-kernels-draft
content:
Purpose and scope

This doc captures our most recent benchmarks and profiling notes comparing INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ quantization strategies across kernels (baseline cuBLAS/GEMM, fused custom CUDA kernels, and optimized matrix-multiply + fused attention kernels). It focuses on the performance/quality tradeoffs for common production workloads (chat generation, single-turn completions, and embedding inference) on A100 and H100 hardware. Goal is to produce clear recommendations for default quant profiles and kernel selection in Redwood serving runtime.

Tested models and hardware
- Models: Llama2-13B, Llama2-70B (decoder-only), Falcon-40B, and an internal distilled 7B.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-40GB, H100-80GB (both single-GPU configs for these runs).
- OS/Stack: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS v12, Triton 2.x for custom kernels, pytorch 2.2 (inference-only), runtime branch: serving/runtime/quant-kernel-experiments.

Workloads and metrics
- Workloads: (1) single-stream chat (seq_len=512 prompt + upto 512 gen), (2) batched inference for many short completions (batch=32, seq_len=128), (3) embeddings (batch=64, seq_len=256).
- Performance metrics: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, memory footprint (GB), and power draw (W).
- Quality metrics: Perplexity (on a held-out dev set), MMLU accuracy (subset), and targeted toxic/formatting regression checks on 200 prompt seeds (binary pass/fail thresholds).

Quantization methods and kernel variants
- INT8 (per-channel weight quantization, symmetric, activations kept in FP16 or FP32 where needed; outlier folding enabled).
- FP8 (E4M3 configuration with block-wise dynamic exponent scaling; intermediate matmuls kept in FP16 where supported).
- GPTQ (8-bit post-training quantization with per-group scaling; retrained zero-shot calibration using 2000 calibration tokens).
- AWQ (approximate weight quantization with mixed integer-fp scales; we used the AWQ v1.1 implementation).
- Kernels: baseline cuBLAS/GEMM (no fusion), fused attention + matmul specialized kernels (Triton), and vendor-optimized fused-kernels (where available).

Key findings (summary)
- Raw throughput: INT8 with optimized fused kernels gives the best tokens/sec for generation on both A100 and H100 (win of 1.4-1.9x vs FP16 baseline depending on model and seq_len). FP8 offers slightly lower throughput than INT8 in our stack (0.9-1.1x of INT8) because FP8 paths are not yet as well optimized in Triton/cuBLAS and fall back to slower pathways for some operators.
- Quality: GPTQ maintains near-baseline quality (<=0.6 perplexity delta, MMLU delta < 1.5% for 13B). AWQ shows mixed results: good compression/perf but occasional outliers in generation (formatting errors) that fail our regression checks (~4% of seeds). INT8 standard quant (no GPTQ/AWQ) shows measurable quality drop for some checkpoints (perplexity delta 1.5-4.0) unless outlier handling and per-channel scales are tuned.
- Kernel interaction: The best results combine carefully calibrated quant (GPTQ or tuned INT8) with fused kernels—fused attention + fused matmul reduces kernel launch overhead and keeps the compute path in the quant-friendly format. Using baseline cuBLAS reduces the realized speedup by half in some cases due to data-format conversion costs.
- Memory footprint: INT8 consistently reduces model memory footprint by ~2x vs FP16, enabling larger batch sizes or longer KV cache. FP8 memory advantage is similar to INT8 in theory, but our FP8 memory path is currently less efficient in end-to-end runtime (extra buffers for exponent handling).

Representative numbers (Llama2-13B, A100, single-GPU, generation workload: prompt 512 + gen 512)
- FP16 baseline (fused kernels): p95 latency = 420 ms, tokens/sec = 3,200, perplexity = 7.8, mem = 26.4 GB
- INT8 (per-channel, tuned, fused kernels): p95 latency = 240 ms, tokens/sec = 5,600, perplexity = 8.4, mem = 13.8 GB
- GPTQ (8-bit GPTQ, fused kernels): p95 latency = 260 ms, tokens/sec = 5,200, perplexity = 7.95, mem = 13.6 GB
- AWQ (AWQ v1.1, fused kernels): p95 latency = 255 ms, tokens/sec = 5,300, perplexity = 8.2, mem = 13.1 GB
- FP8 (E4M3, current implementation): p95 latency = 300 ms, tokens/sec = 4,500, perplexity = 8.0, mem = 14.0 GB

Notes on profiling and where the wins/losses come from
- NVTX tagging + Nsight Systems revealed that non-fused GEMM + attention operator boundaries cause a lot of host/device synchronization. Fusing attention with matmul reduces CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and improves kernel GPU-occupancy -> primary source of p95 reduction.
- Data-format casts (FP16 <-> INT8 staging) are non-trivial: our baseline path had extra reorder kernels that nullified up to 20% of raw matmul speed gains. Optimized kernels that consume quantized weights and produce quantized activations avoid conversions and are crucial.
- FP8 implementation currently incurs extra exponent handling passes on CPU (preprocessing) for our Triton kernels; moving exponent scaling to a tiny GPU kernel removes ~10-15% overhead in later experiments.

Quality observations and failure modes
- GPTQ: best quality-preserving 8-bit method in our experiments. It requires a calibration step (representative token set) and has a small runtime cost in quant table lookups, but that overhead is offset by throughput gains. GPTQ sometimes underperforms on extremely long-range factuality tests (70B showed larger degradation than 13B), so we recommend per-model checks.
- AWQ: good memory+perf, but exhibits instability on some attention patterns (rare token emissions or repeated loops) – these showed up in our 200-prompt regression suite. AWQ tuning can reduce failures but increases dev ops complexity.
- INT8 naive: without per-channel/scaling and outlier folding the quality regression is significant for some layers (especially embeddings and final lm_head). Use of per-channel scales + outlier clipping is required for production.

Recommendations (short-term)
- Default production profile (hosted API): GPTQ-8 + fused kernels for Llama2-13B family. Provides near-FP16 quality with ~2x tokens/sec and ~2x memory reduction.
- Large models (>=70B): prefer cautiously tuned INT8 or FP8 with extensive regression tests; enable automatic rollback/fallback to FP16 or GPTQ-quantized variant if quality alerts trigger.
- Embeddings path: aggressive INT8 is acceptable (few quality regressions observed) — choose tuned per-channel quant and enable a small calibration check on signup.
- Kernel priority: ship fused-quant-aware kernels in the runtime and avoid conversion-heavy fallback paths. If FP8 becomes vendor-supported (cuBLAS/Triton native), re-evaluate to potentially prefer FP8 for some workloads because FP8 has native dynamic-range benefits for transformers.

Operational notes and action items (TODOs)
- TODO: Add automated calibration flow in the serving control plane that runs a 2k-token calibration sample for GPTQ during model onboarding (owner: Priya).
- TODO: Wire GPU Nsight logs into the console perf dashboards for model+kernel telemetry (owner: Diego). Capture kernel occupancy, mem bandwidth, and time spent in reorders.
- TODO: Create a canary rollout policy that initially serves 5% of traffic with GPTQ-int8 fused kernel config and monitor perplexity + user-facing regressions (owner: Lena).
- TODO: Optimize FP8 kernel exponent handling on-GPU (experimental patch in PR #678).

Caveats and open questions
- Our FP8 implementation was constrained by Triton/cuBLAS support and likely underestimates FP8 potential once vendor paths are optimized. Re-run baseline after vendor FP8 primitives are available.
- Long-term prefer a matrix: (model size x quant method) -> recommended kernel + fallback policy. We need a stable evaluation matrix and automated weekly re-benchmarking.

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing these numbers
1) Checkout branch: serving/runtime/quant-kernel-experiments
2) Setup: CUDA 12.1, Nsight 2025.3, PyTorch 2.2, Triton 2.x
3) Calibration sets: use s3://redwood-bench/calibration/gptq-2k-toks/{llama2-13b, llama2-70b}
4) Benchmark script: scripts/bench/quant_bench.py --model $MODEL --quant $METHOD --kernel $KERNEL --batch $BATCH --seq $SEQ --device a100
5) Collect NVTX traces: nvtx_trace.py wraps runs and emits .nsys for upload to perf-dashboard

If you're reviewing: please check the representative numbers and failure examples attached in the linked artifacts. Feedback wanted on: acceptable regression thresholds for MMLU and perplexity, and whether AWQ should be gated behind an opt-in trial.

-- Avery
